When writing comprehensive language manuals for ls_bench, start by reading the existing stub to understand current state. The Fortran manual required replacing a 54-line stub with ~300 lines covering: C interoperability for POSIX directory operations (opendir/readdir/closedir), stat struct mapping, string intrinsics (trim/len_trim/index/scan/verify/transfer), date_and_time for timestamps, CLI argument parsing, error handling via iostat/iomsg, sorting via C qsort interop, and locale via setlocale interop. Key insight: Modern Fortran (F2003+) is powerful for systems programming through iso_c_binding, but lacks native directory/stat APIs—C interop is essential. When documenting C interop, always show both the interface block and example usage. The date_and_time intrinsic returns an 8-element array, not an epoch—epoch conversion requires C localtime() interop. F2023 adds is_directory to inquire(). error stop (F2008) is preferred over stop for immediate termination. qsort comparison functions MUST be bind(c).

CRITICAL: Skills sandbox in pillywiggins has zero OS-level isolation. Permission flags (network, subprocess, file_write) are honor-system only — set as env vars with no enforcement. Subprocess runs as same UID, has full filesystem read, and can make arbitrary network connections regardless of "permissions" config. Docker Compose has no security_opt, no cap_drop, no resource limits. Skills in shared volume can poison all agents.

Comprehensive Fortran manual for ls_bench covers F2003/F2008/F2023 APIs. Key insight: modern Fortran has no native directory iterator or stat; must use iso_c_binding to POSIX opendir/readdir/closedir and stat structs. F2023 adds inquire(..., is_directory=) which was previously only available via C interop. String handling uses trim/len_trim/index/scan/verify. No built-in sorting or locale; qsort via C interop is standard. date_and_time returns values(8) but has no epoch conversion; must use C localtime() for file timestamps.

When updating docker-compose.yaml.example healthchecks: check if curl/wget is available in the image. python:3.12-slim does not include curl by default. Use `python -c 'import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8080/healthz");'` as a robust fallback. Always add `start_period: 30s` for agent services to allow time for startup before healthchecks begin failing.

Dockerfile security hardening pattern for pillywiggins: 1) Create non-root user with `RUN useradd -m appuser && mkdir -p /app/logs && chown -R appuser:appuser /app` before USER directive. 2) Add HEALTHCHECK using `CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/healthz')" || exit 1`. 3) Set `USER appuser` as the last directive before CMD. For docker-compose.yaml.example, every service should have: cap_drop: [ALL], read_only: true, no_new_privileges: true, tmpfs: [/tmp], deploy.resources.limits.memory, restart: unless-stopped, and healthcheck. Services with volumes need tmpfs for writable /tmp. The test pattern uses yaml.safe_load to parse the compose file and validates these fields exist on all infrastructure services.

Channel adapter security audit findings: (1) CRITICAL - Telegram command handlers bypass _is_authorized() because they are registered as telegram.ext CommandHandlers which fire before MessageHandler where auth check lives. This allows any user to execute /status, /models, /model, /skills, /compact, /reset, /help without authorization. (2) HIGH - Discord command methods (_cmd_help, _cmd_status, etc.) are dead code, never called from _on_message. (3) HIGH - Slack adapter logs first 10 chars of bot_token on connect, partial credential exposure. (4) HIGH - Email adapter concatenates user-controlled Subject into reply, potential header injection via newline characters. (5) HIGH - Authorization check fails for non-integer user IDs on Slack/Matrix/Email because Settings.get_allowed_user_ids() returns set[int] via int(uid.strip()), but BaseAdapter._is_authorized() converts to str comparison - however Slack user IDs are alphanumeric like U07ABCDEF, Matrix IDs are @user:server, and emails are strings, all of which fail int() conversion, silently setting _allowed_user_ids to empty set and denying all users. (6) HIGH - Email adapter normalizes message timestamp to datetime.now() instead of parsing actual msg.date, also uses unsafe re.sub for HTML stripping (DoS risk with large HTML). (7) MEDIUM - Discord and Telegram log first 80 chars of user message content, potential PII exposure. (8) MEDIUM - No rate limiting on any adapter. (9) MEDIUM - Email import html inside method body on every call. (10) MEDIUM - Matrix adapter calls asyncio.create_task for each message without task tracking, potential runaway task accumulation. (11) LOW - Deprecated asyncio.get_event_loop() in config.py line 109.

When brain tools create a fresh Settings() instance on every tool call, EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto triggers Ollama model discovery repeatedly, causing significant latency per embedding call. The fix is to resolve embedding config once at agent startup and pass the resolved values (model, dimension, base_url, provider, api_key) through the AgentDeps dataclass that is already injected into every tool call via RunContext. This avoids re-reading .env and avoids any discovery logic in the hot path. Key change: _embed_text should accept explicit keyword arguments instead of a Settings object, and all AgentDeps construction sites (base.py, scheduler.py) must populate the new fields from the agent's own _settings instance.

When writing OCaml manuals for ls-bench, the Unix module is central for file metadata (stat/lstat), directory handles (opendir/readdir/closedir), and permission/type checks. The stdlib lacks strftime, so date formatting must be manual via Unix.localtime + Printf.sprintf. String.starts_with is 4.13+; for older OCaml versions use name.[0] <> '.'. For locale-aware sorting, Camomile is the standard external library. Always include quick reference using Sys.readdir + Unix.lstat + st_kind pattern matching.

Fix event loop mismatch in skill sandbox: In the subprocess sandbox wrappers (_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE and _TEST_DRIVEN_WRAPPER in sandbox.py), we added a block that ensures a current event loop exists before skill code is loaded. This resolves the issue where skills using asyncio.get_event_loop() (deprecated but common in LLM-generated code) failed with RuntimeError: no current event loop in the sandbox, while working fine in production. The wrapper now tries get_running_loop() first and, if no loop is running, creates a new one and sets it. This is backward-compatible with skills that already use get_running_loop(). We also added tests to verify both get_event_loop() and get_running_loop() work inside the sandbox.

In ls-bench, adding a new tool test suite (find) follows the same black-box runner pattern as ls. Key steps: 1) Extend runner.py with a FindRunner (or generic runner) that discovers candidate via FIND_CANDIDATE env var and compares stdout/stderr/exit against system reference. 2) Write generate_<tool>_fixtures.sh to create deterministic /tmp/<tool>_fixture tree with the file types/sizes/mtimes needed by spec. 3) In test file, set FIXTURE = Path('/tmp/find_fixture') and inherit from base class that provides run_and_compare(). Use sort_stdout where order may vary (e.g., unordered exec). 4) For destructive tests like -delete, create separate temp trees for reference and candidate and compare after setup. 5) Run self-test mode (FIND_TEST_MODE=self) to validate harness before any candidate exists.

Coverage audit learnings for Pillywiggins: 1) Adapter async runtime paths (Matrix/Slack/Email) are the biggest blind spots (~39-46% coverage). Future audits should start by mocking external SDKs (nio, slack_bolt, aiosmtplib) rather than waiting for full coverage data. 2) `pytest --collect-only` with 1,500+ tests can be slow; faster to run with `-k` exclusions for real external deps. 3) The 85% total coverage metric hides critical adapter gaps. Always audit per-module coverage before trusting aggregate numbers. 4) Branch coverage would have revealed even more issues in async error paths; recommend enabling `--cov-branch` if future audits are needed.

When writing language manuals for ls-bench, target ~250-300 lines of markdown. For C#, the key namespaces are System.IO (Directory, DirectoryInfo, FileInfo, FileSystemInfo, FileAttributes, Path), System.Linq (OrderBy, ThenBy), System.Globalization (CultureInfo), and System.Threading (CurrentThread.CurrentCulture). The FileSystemInfo base class pattern (is FileInfo / is DirectoryInfo) is the idiomatic way to handle mixed entries. For GNU ls date formatting, the 6-month threshold check uses TotalDays > 180. The Mono.Unix.UnixFileInfo class provides Unix permissions/uid/gid on Mono/Linux but requires the Mono.Posix NuGet package on modern .NET.

Built ls-bench black-box test suite in Python stdlib unittest (no pytest dependency because pytest was not installed in env). Key decisions:
1. Used `unittest` instead of `pytest` to avoid dependency issues.
2. `runner.py` discovers candidates via LS_CANDIDATE env var or reference/*/ls and bench/*/ls.
3. `generate_fixtures.sh` uses deterministic `touch -d` for mtimes; creates symlinks, FIFO (mkfifo), unicode and control-char filenames, 255-byte filename, size gradient files, empty dir.
4. Self-test mode (LS_TEST_MODE=self) compares reference ls against itself to validate harness without a candidate binary.
5. `run_and_compare` supports `ignore_stderr`, `ignore_exitcode`, `normalise_times`, and `env` overrides.
6. Time normalisation regex matches long-format time column to avoid `.` / `..` flakiness; note actual `st_mtime` for `.` and `..` is the fixture dir's own mtime, not controlled by `touch -d`, but that's fine because we compare candidate vs reference on the same filesystem.
7. Block device (`mknod b`) is not supported in user namespaces, so no blockdev fixture is created; FIFO is used instead.
8. Total line presence/absence tests assert correct POSIX behavior per spec §4.2.6.

Cross-agent routing integration test pattern for Pillywiggin: When testing a pipeline from UnifiedMessage → AgentDeps → brain.run() → send_message_to_agent tool → NATS publish_direct, the cleanest approach is to mock the brain.run() method on the agent, then inside that mock call send_message_to_agent(ctx) directly with the captured deps from the call_args. Use positional call_args[0][0] for the user_prompt kwarg, and construct a FakeRunContext class that wraps the deps object. This avoids dealing with pydantic-ai's RunContext internals (tool registration, message history, etc.). Example: `class FakeRunContext: def __init__(self, deps): self.deps = deps`.

Additionally, when sending messages to another agent via NATS, the routing_info must preserve all original user metadata (channel_user_id, metadata dict, conversation_key, channel) so that the receiving agent can route replies back to the correct user. The metadata dict especially needs to handle nested values and empty dicts correctly.

sandbox.py error reporting fix: When editing multi-line triple-quoted wrapper templates that get written to temp files, be extremely careful with backslash escaping. `\\n` means literal `\n` inside the generated file. Also, the prompt sanitizer can block innocent stderr text (e.g., containing 'warn!'), so tests that assert raw sandbox error strings should monkeypatch `_sanitize_sandbox_result` to identity. Fixes to reference/find/find.py for 7 targeted test failures:

1. Parser precedence: Implemented two-level grammar (_parse_or -> _parse_and -> _parse_not -> _parse_primary) so implicit -and binds tighter than -o. Required because `(-name alpha -prune -o -print)` must parse as `((-name alpha) -and (-prune)) -o (-print)` for GNU find compatibility.

2. Default print suppression logic: Added _has_any_explicit_action() that walks the entire AST. If any explicit action exists anywhere (PrintNode, PruneNode, DeleteNode, ExecNode), default print is suppressed globally. This allows pruned items to match a branch with no explicit print and still be printed.

3. -delete traversal order: Changed FindWalker._visit to perform directory deletion AFTER descending into children when delete_mode is True. Post-order deletion prevents "No such file or directory" errors when empty inner directories are removed before their parents.

4. UserNode/GroupNode error handling: Modified _resolve_user/_resolve_group to return triples (id, ok, is_numeric). Walk the expression tree before traversal to emit stderr warnings and set exit code 1 for unknown non-numeric user/group names, matching GNU find behavior.

For Go ls-bench manual: filepath.WalkDirFunc signature is func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error (not filepath.WalkDirFunc as a type name in signatures). Use fs.SkipDir (from io/fs) to skip directories. Go stdlib has no built-in uid/gid name lookup; must use os/user or external calls. time.Format uses reference time Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006. For GNU ls date display, threshold is 6 months: recent uses "Jan _2 15:04", old uses "Jan _2  2006".

Pillywiggins Infrastructure Security Audit (cell--yqe5z-mp0oyvztwg7) completed by QuickDawn on 2026-05-11. 19 findings across CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW severity. CRITICAL: NATS runs with anonymous access (no auth, no TLS). Hardcoded DB passwords 'changeme' in init-db.sql, config.py, env.example. Docker containers run as root with no USER directive. HIGH: No container resource limits (CPU/memory). Redis has no password/ACL. No capability dropping or read-only rootfs. Health endpoint binds to 0.0.0.0 and discloses internal component status. Scheduler reads JSON from disk and executes arbitrary prompts via _builtin_custom. init-db.sql uses hnsw index while setup-db.sh uses ivfflat. MEDIUM: Flat Docker network. env.example comments expose config details. Ollama runs externally with no auth - any container on network can access it. config.py has plaintext defaults. LOW: Dockerfile pre-installs runtime packages. docker-compose bind-mounts skills dir read-write. 5 documented-but-unimplemented hardening items in overview-v2.md.

SKILL_META can be written by LLMs (like Puck) as either a Python dict assignment (SKILL_META = {...}) or as comments (# SKILL_META = {...} or # SKILL_META\n# name: ...). The registry originally only handled the dict assignment via getattr and a comment block parser for key:value lines. We added inline dict parsing to _extract_meta_from_comments to handle the # SKILL_META = {...} format. Key learnings: 1) Single quotes in comment dicts must be normalized to double quotes before json.loads. 2) The inline dict parser must only trigger when '=' is present to avoid confusing with block header # SKILL_META. 3) Malformed inline dicts must gracefully return empty so the 'no SKILL_META' warning still fires. This prevents silent registration of broken skills.

ls-bench now supports 3 commands: ls, find, grep. All reference implementations pass tests:
- LS: 58 tests OK (1 skipped - uid_fallback requires root)
- FIND: 65 tests OK (1 skipped - block device requires root)
- GREP: 82 tests OK (0 skipped)

Key fixes for new commands:
1. **find boolean operators**: `-or` has lower precedence than `-and`. Implemented with precedence-climbing parser: _parse_or → _parse_and → _parse_not → _parse_primary.
2. **find prune**: Prevents descending but still evaluates the matched directory itself for printing/actions.
3. **find delete**: Post-order traversal so children are deleted before parents. Only delete empty directories.
4. **find exec**: `;` = one invocation per file replacing {}; `+` = batch mode appending all paths as trailing arguments.
5. **find ownership**: Numeric UID/GID comparison even when names don't exist in /etc/passwd.
6. **grep last-flag-wins**: Output mode priority (-l/-L > -c > normal). Regex mode conflicts (both -E and -F given = error).
7. **grep directory handling**: Directory without -r prints "Is a directory" to stderr but doesn't affect exit code for other files.

Total tests: 58 + 65 + 82 = 205 tests across 3 commands.

Benchmark runner supports: ls, find, grep with per-command timeouts and env var injection.

Lua manual for ls-bench: replaced stub with comprehensive guide covering lfs (LuaFileSystem) and core stdlib. Key gotchas: (1) lfs.dir returns a closure, not a direct iterator; must handle . and .. manually. (2) Lua patterns use % for escapes, not \ like regex. (3) os.date("%b %d %H:%M") zero-pads day; GNU ls space-pads—requires post-processing gsub(" 0", "  "). (4) string.compare does not exist; use < operator. (5) os.setlocale("", "collate") affects sort order. Target length ~250-300 non-empty lines; final file has 268 non-empty lines.

When writing grep spec for ls-bench: Follow the same structural style as spec/ls.md (Overview -> Synopsis -> Supported Flags -> Output Formatting -> Edge Cases -> Concrete Examples -> Testability Requirements -> References). For grep specifically, be very precise about BRE vs ERE escaping differences (e.g., \| in BRE vs | in ERE), the '-w' word boundary rules (word constituents are [A-Za-z0-9_]), and the fact that -r implies -H (file name prefix always shown). GNU find -exec '{}' semantics: The placeholder '{}' only gets substituted when it is an isolated argument token. A literal single brace '{' is treated as a normal argument and is not substituted. This means `-exec basename { \;` runs `basename {` for each file, while `-exec basename {} \;` substitutes the file path.

For the '+' terminator, GNU find requires '{}' to be present in the command; otherwise it errors with "missing argument to `-exec'" (exit code 1) regardless of whether any files match.

When invoking -exec commands, stdout/stderr should be passed through (not captured), because test harnesses compare them against the reference find output.

Error-message prefix for a Python-based reference find must match the system find binary path used by the test runner (e.g. /usr/bin/find), not just "find:". Use shutil.which("find") or the like to get the canonical path for the prefix.

GNU find expression parser precedence fix: _parse_tokens was left-recursive with equal precedence for -and and -or, causing -or to bind tighter than implicit -and (or left-to-right). Fix: decomposed into precedence-climbing layers: _parse_or > _parse_and (with implicit -and) > _parse_not > _parse_primary. This matches GNU find precedence: -not (highest), then -and (implicit/juxtaposition), then -or (lowest). Parenthesized expressions parsed at _parse_or level so operators inside parens follow same precedence.

When writing reference manuals for AI agents implementing Unix tools, include both a kernel/syscall layer (what the OS guarantees) and a libc wrapper layer (what the agent actually calls). Key gotchas for `ls`: (1) `readdir` d_type is unreliable—must fall back to `lstat` when `DT_UNKNOWN`. (2) `readlink` returns untargeted, unterminated strings—agent must null-terminate manually. (3) `localtime` uses static storage; thread-safe agents need `localtime_r`. (4) `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` can fail with ENOTTY when piped; always check `isatty` and fall back to `COLUMNS` env var. (5) `setlocale(LC_ALL,"")` is required for locale-aware sorting and time formatting; otherwise everything defaults to C locale.

When writing a spec document for ls-bench, follow the same structure as spec/ls.md: (1) overview/synopsis, (2) table of supported flags/predicates, (3) detailed semantics and edge cases, (4) concrete examples with a fixed fixture tree, (5) testability requirements, (6) references. Use absolute paths in examples for determinism. Match GNU behavior as the reference. Use `\u003e` and `\u0026` entities to avoid XML issues when storing.

When writing comprehensive language manuals for ls_bench, start by reading the existing stub to understand current state. The Fortran manual required replacing a 54-line stub with ~300 lines covering: C interoperability for POSIX directory operations (opendir/readdir/closedir), stat struct mapping, string intrinsics (trim/len_trim/index/scan/verify/transfer), date_and_time for timestamps, CLI argument parsing, error handling via iostat/iomsg, sorting via C qsort interop, and locale via setlocale interop. Key insight: Modern Fortran (F2003+) is powerful for systems programming through iso_c_binding, but lacks native directory/stat APIs—C interop is essential. When documenting C interop, always show both the interface block and example usage. The date_and_time intrinsic returns an 8-element array, not an epoch—epoch conversion requires C localtime() interop. F2023 adds is_directory to inquire(). error stop (F2008) is preferred over stop for immediate termination. qsort comparison functions MUST be bind(c).

Cross-agent routing fix pattern for Pillywiggins: When forwarding messages between agents via NATS, always preserve original user routing metadata (channel_user_id, conversation_key, metadata) in a routing_info dict within the NATS payload. The receiving agent should check routing_info and use its own adapter.send() to reply directly to the user if the channel matches, instead of replying via NATS which traps responses in agent-to-agent loops. AgentDeps must be updated with new fields (channel_user_id, metadata) and ALL construction sites must pass these values from the original UnifiedMessage.

ls-bench v1 is complete. Key coordination learnings:

1. **Chunked manual format works well for LLM context efficiency**: Splitting OS and C library manuals into 30-100 line per-topic files (manuals/kernel/*.md, manuals/libc/*.md) with README index lets agents selectively load only what they need. The original monolithic files remain as authoritative reference.

2. **Feature-based decomposition with document-first approach succeeded**: Spawned spec writer → OS manual writer → chunked manual restructure → (parallel) language manuals + test suite + templates + envs + ref implementations + runner. The document-first approach (write specs and manuals before code) is natural for benchmark frameworks.

3. **14-language gradient provides meaningful capability measurement**: Ordered by exoticness (Python → JS → C → C++ → Java → C# → Rust → Perl → Go → Lua → Zig → Haskell → OCaml → Fortran), this gives clear per-language scores that help select models/agents for specific language domains.

4. **Black-box test harness with self-test mode is robust**: The test suite compares candidate `ls` output against reference using the system `ls` as ground truth, which means it validates itself even when no reference implementations exist yet.

5. **Make run target must discover and build subdirectories**: Top-level Makefile uses $(wildcard reference/*) and $(wildcard bench/*) with per-directory Makefiles. This pattern scales naturally for new commands.

6. **Worker coordination with sqlite_busy retries**: When hive cells are locked, retry after a short delay works. Sequential closing after batch operations prevents most lock contention.
